newsitem.title: HONG KONG: British missions stop taking HK visa applications.
newsitem.headline: British missions stop taking HK visa applications.

text.p: British diplomatic missions around the world stopped accepting applications for Hong Kong visas on Saturday because of the British colony's imminent return to Chinese rule, the local government said on Saturday.

"In view of the change of sovereignty of Hong Kong on July 1, all British embassies, high commissions and consulates will accept applications for visas for Hong Kong up to May 30 this year," the Immigration Department said in a statement. It said the move was necessary to ensure that all of the visa applications for Hong Kong accepted by British posts could be processed before the handover.
Britain hands the territory back to China on July 1, ending more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
Nationals of more than 170 countries can visit the territory without visas. Only nationals from 23 countries and stateless people need to apply for a visa before their visit.
Foreign visitors can continue to submit their visa applications directly to the Immigration Department either by post or through a local sponsor, the statement said.
